tasks.commitBody: The event page gains a series picker that tells the truth about what changing a series costs. An event inherits up to four fields from its series — name, duration, location, description — whenever it carries none of its own, so reassigning can rewrite four things on screen at once and unassigning a series child leaves it nameless by design. The picker names the fields this event actually inherits, computed from raw property presence rather than displayed blankness because a stored empty string blocks inheritance while looking identical, and shows what they will become before the write; an event inheriting nothing changes series with no ceremony at all. On the wire the change targets the series parent value id alone — reassignment through the atomic-overwrite primitive, unassignment through a single value delete — because an event's parent property also holds its season, and a blanket replace would move the event between seasons as a side effect. Nothing is copied onto the event to soften the loss: that would quietly stop the event tracking its series, which is a different feature and a stated choice we did not make. The write is server-confirmed per the truthful-state rule; failure keeps the previous series selected and says so. #233 seam: this shipped first — #233's enumeration of event-name read sites must include this feature. The rights shape follows the probe branch recorded in the stated choices, per the PO ruling on the issue. STATED CHOICES: <GREEN agent fills>.
